fns.desc: hostapd_parse_link_reconf_req_sta_profile: 'sta_info = per_sta_prof->variable;' (== buf+4) then immediately 'if (*sta_info > end - sta_info)' dereferences *sta_info WITHOUT first checking that at least 1 byte remains at that offset. The only earlier length check (line 2114, 'len < sizeof(*elem) + 2UL') only guarantees len >= 4, i.e. end == buf+4 == sta_info is a valid (boundary) case -- when an attacker sends a Per-STA Profile subelement whose declared length (sub_elem_len+2, wire-controlled from the Reconfiguration MLE) is exactly 4, sta_info == end and '*sta_info' reads 1 byte past the subelement's validated length before the length is itself checked. Likely non-crashing in practice (mlbuf's real allocation is usually larger than one subelement), but a genuine out-of-bounds-relative-to-validated-length read on attacker-controlled wire data.
